body:
MYK'S QUESTION OPENS THIS, because every future reader will ask it (2026-07-26): "don't we get this for free from GraphQL, `Ticket(id)` vs `Ticket()`?" The spelling IS free — the generator could emit `tickets(limit, after)` tomorrow. The answer is not, because the question is what RESOLVES it. An entity has no type: any entity reads through any registered lens, and the federation story depends on that staying true. The type lives in the vocabulary's layers, and the layering is Myk's own correction (2026-07-26): "the type is what the SCHEMA defines — it's the type of the view. A hyperschema's type describes a hyperview." HyperSchema : HyperView :: Schema : View — so 'which entities are BoardItems' is an evidence-level question (whose claims does the gather select), and 'what does a BoardItem look like' is per-reading, answered only through a schema.

THE EVIDENCE this ticket exists on: the board (T108/§34) dogfooded into the gap WITHIN THE HOUR. A renderer renders one entity's node, GraphQL queries one entity, and nothing enumerates "all BoardItems." The live v1 board improvised a singleton `board:main` with one claim per dynamic item context — invisible to the typed GraphQL surface and to `writable`, so writes had to ride /append. The durable §34 shape pays the other price: explicit membership (`boardAdd`), a second call per item and a collection that only knows what was filed through it. Both are workarounds for the same missing door.

THE SHAPE, DECIDED (Myk, 2026-07-26). Candidate resolvers, costed: (a) scan-the-ground-per-query is H8's named hazard and T37's bug class — refused; (b) "a maintained index is a subsystem" — the objection DISSOLVES, because (c) containers already ARE governed, erasure-reachable, freezable maintained sets. So: THE MATERIALIZATION IS A CONTAINER. Back the hyperschema with a container whose membership Term is the gather's selection, following the ground live — his words: "if we backed a hyperschema with a container such that every time a new delta came in it was selected we'd have a container that had a pre-filtered list." The container backs the HYPERSCHEMA (evidence-level membership: which entities have relevant claims, bucketed how), and because one hyperschema serves many schemas, that single maintained candidate set feeds EVERY lens reading over it. The DOOR is per-lens: `tickets()` returns view-typed answers whose shape depends on which schema you asked through. One container, N collection doors. The §14 edge rides along as friendly context: an entity can hold evidence yet resolve sparse under a given schema — the door returns views, and absence stays absence.

SCOPE, MYK'S CALL (2026-07-26): AUTHED DOOR ONLY in v1. "Right now don't worry about strangers — be aware of what we're doing, but we are the only current user, and I'm more interested in a working app than the fully general case." A token holder already reads everything point-wise, so an authed listing widens nothing — convenience over served data, ordinary landing, build tier. PUBLIC enumeration is EXPLICITLY DEFERRED, seen and named: enumeration is exactly what the uniform-404 discipline prevents elsewhere, a public listing door can inventory a store, and the eventual design is a per-lens `enumerable` flag on the public declaration, DEFAULT NO (a blog wants its index public; an address book must not be crawlable). That is §12's question and it waits for a customer.

TWO OPEN ITEMS FOR THE BUILD, named as such: (a) members are deltas, so the door projects DISTINCT ENTITIES from the member set — the same byTargetContext grouping move, plus pagination; (b) MEASURE whether live membership (`watch`) maintains incrementally or re-evaluates per pulse — T37's lesson is that "re-resolved live" can spell "full scan per request," and that measurement decides whether this design is honest at scale.

ADJACENCY: T91/T93 own the container `members()` surface this rides on; the board (§34) is the first customer — its `boardAdd`/membership workaround retires the day `boardItems()` answers.
title: The listing door — a kind's entities, served: container-backed enumeration for the authed door
